## Verdict

**The mapping feature got built, and the module works.** Every headline finding from round 1 is
fixed. An analyzer code binds to a real catalog test through the GUI, from the whole 183-test
catalog, with LOINC shown. The profile no longer applies partially and silently — unresolved codes
carry an explicit `mappingState` and can be mapped or excluded. The sign-off is a recorded artefact
with a signer and a timestamp, pinned to a `bindingFingerprint` *and* a `recognitionFingerprint`, so
it goes stale when either changes. QC is no longer coupled to activation. And the analyzer lifecycle
runs end to end: activate → deactivate → reactivate, from the API and from the UI, with no hard
Delete anywhere. **Twelve of thirteen round-1 findings closed.**

**The 2026-08-27 retest closed four more and opened four.** Δ-K (no data-flow control), Δ-W (the type
picker does not filter) and the dead-end *Needs Attention* card are fixed outright; Δ-S's
data-integrity risk is fixed and leaves a minor UX residue; and results now carry real provenance in
the payload. What the same run found is
that the two paths a lab would use to *repair* a mapping problem do not hold up: **Duplicate Profile
discards every mapping decision and silently drops the unresolved value that motivated the fork**
(Δ-AA), **the Analyzer Types catalog reports a profile as `COMPLETE` while it is holding patient
results and never updates when the mapping is fixed** (Δ-AB), **an analyzer code the profile does
not declare has no resolution path at all** (Δ-AC), and **a confirmed mapping change is not
audited** (Δ-AD).

**Nothing here is a release blocker,** but the shape of the remaining work has changed. Round 2
closed the *build-it* gaps; what is left are *operate-it* gaps — Δ-R (operational QC cannot be
configured at all, third round unchanged), the repair paths above, and one dead end in the
"my instrument isn't listed" flow (Δ-Y). Δ-AB is the one to weigh most carefully, because it makes a
supervisor's at-a-glance view of mapping health actively wrong rather than merely incomplete.

**Maturity: M3.** Instrument, the mapping editor and the lifecycle all round-trip through a second
surface, and the mapping cross-links to the real test catalog. REPORTABLE is not evidenced — but
only because result ingestion needs the analyzer simulator, which this instance does not have.
Standing up that simulator is now the highest-value next step for this module, because it is the
only thing between OGC-1057 and a reportable grade.

**Recommendation: mergeable.** Δ-R and Δ-AB are worth landing first; neither blocks the others.

## A finding this report withdraws — please read before acting on the review submission

The in-app review (**submission id 16**) records **step 5 "Activate the analyzer" as Fail**, and an
earlier draft of this report led with a blocker: *"`activation-readiness` returns `ready:true` while
`POST /activate` returns 500, deterministically, reproduced on a second analyzer."*

**That finding is wrong and is withdrawn.** It came from hand-rolled `POST`s during the interactive
walkthrough that omitted this build's CSRF header. Every non-GET REST call on 3.2.2.0 must carry
`X-CSRF-Token`, whose value lives in `localStorage.CSRF`; without it the server answers
`403 {"message":"CSRF token missing or invalid"}`.

With the header, on analyzers **363** and **364**, repeatedly and in both directions:

```
POST /rest/analyzer/analyzers/363/activate    → 200  {"status":"ACTIVE","activated":true,"blockers":[]}
POST /rest/analyzer/analyzers/363/deactivate  → 200  {"status":"INACTIVE","deactivated":true}
POST /rest/analyzer/analyzers/363/reactivate  → 200  {"status":"ACTIVE","activated":true}
```

The UI agrees. *Connect → Finish and activate* issues `PUT …/364` **200** then
`POST …/364/activate` **200**, and the row flips to **Active**. The row menu's *Deactivate* returns
**200** and the row flips to **Inactive**; *Reactivate* — offered only on inactive rows — returns
**200** and it flips back. All four paths are now guarded by tests that pass.

**Δ-U ("reactivate is untestable") is withdrawn with it.** Reactivate works.

Two honest caveats. First, a request without the header returns 403, not 500, so the 500s the
walkthrough saw are not fully explained by the missing header alone — either the build changed under
us between ~16:20 and ~18:15 UTC, or the probe was malformed in a second way. Second, the UI banners
observed at the time (*"Deactivation failed — Internal Server Error"*, *"Analyzer readiness could not
be checked"*) were real observations that no longer reproduce. **Either way the defect does not
reproduce and should not be filed.** If anyone has already started on it, stop.

The lasting lesson is a harness rule, now recorded in the QA repo: *a write that omits CSRF does not
merely fail — it manufactures a finding.*

## Δ ledger

### Δ-R — the New Control Lot form cannot be saved at all **(revised — this is not what round 1 found)**

Round 1 reported this as *hidden validation*: the form POSTed, the server answered
`400 "Manufacturer fixed method requires both mean and standard deviation"`, and the banner said
only *"Failed to save control lot"*. **On 3.2.2.0 that is no longer the defect.** The form now
issues **no request at all**, so there is nothing for the UI to surface and setting Mean/SD changes
nothing. The finding is an **unwired Save**, not a validation-messaging problem — the earlier
framing in this report and in the in-app review has been corrected accordingly.

**Observed.** With every field populated — lot number, control material, control level, expiration
date, analyzer, test, Active, and Mean 25.00 / SD 2.50 set through *Statistics Configuration* —
clicking **Save**:
- issues **no network request** (verified with the browser's own network recorder),
- logs **no console error or exception**,
- marks **no field invalid** and shows **no message**,
- does not navigate, and
- leaves `GET /rest/qc/control-lots` unchanged.

**The handler is wired but bails.** Save is `type="submit"`, enabled, inside a real `<form>` that
carries a React `onSubmit` function. So the submit path exists and returns before issuing anything.

**Endpoint probe.**
```
GET  /rest/qc/control-lots  → 200  [ the seeded lot ]      ← list endpoint, works
POST /rest/qc/control-lots  → 405  Method Not Supported     ← no create handler at this path
POST /rest/qc/controlLot    → 400  (exists, different DTO)
```
The list and the create endpoints live at different paths (`/qc/control-lots` vs `/qc/controlLot`),
which may be part of why nothing is wired up.

**Revalidation** (per the QA repo's bug-revalidation protocol):
- **Method A — fresh tab: CONFIRMED.** New tab, fresh login (new session id and CSRF), navigated by
  **sidebar** (Analyzers → Quality Control → Control Lots) and entered through the canonical
  **New Control Lot** button rather than a direct URL, all interaction by real mouse click.
- **Method B — full re-login: CONFIRMED.** That run began at `/login` in a clean session.
- **Method C — endpoint probe:** as above.
- **Tooling ruled out:** the network recorder captured `GET /rest/qc/control-lots → 200` on the same
  tab moments later, so "zero requests on Save" is a real observation, not a capture gap.
- Reproduced across two tabs, two sessions, two entry paths, two analyzer/test combinations, with
  and without Mean/SD, and via synthetic click, real mouse click and Enter-key submit.
- **Re-confirmed 2026-08-27** on a fresh seed, in a fresh tab, with the network recorder cleared
  immediately before the click: the Save produced **zero REST requests of any kind**.

**Also on this form: the Test picker is not scoped to the selected analyzer.** With *Cepheid
GeneXpert (ASTM Mode)* chosen, the Test dropdown offers all **183** OpenELIS tests — ALT(Serum),
AMACR, Actin Smooth Muscle and so on. GeneXpert maps four (395 Xpert MTB/RIF, 396 Xpert RIF
Resistance, 313 HIV Viral Load, 300 COVID-19 PCR). A lot bound to a test the analyzer never reports
would never be evaluated by any Westgard rule. Worth fixing in the same pass as the Save.

**Consequence.** Operational QC cannot be configured at all: control lots cannot be created, and
**Rule Configuration has no create control** ("No rule configurations found", nothing to add one).

Severity: **High.** It is not a release blocker — activation deliberately does not depend on QC
(see AC-9) — but a lab cannot run quality control, and it is now the **third round in a row** this
surface has shipped broken.

### Δ-S — Add Analyzer does not reset the setup panel **— the data-integrity defect is FIXED; a UX residue remains. Retested 2026-08-27**

Reported as: with an analyzer open (row menu → *Edit setup*), clicking **Add Analyzer** dropped
`analyzerId` from the URL — the panel *looked* fresh — but retained the previous analyzer's values
*and its identity*, so Continue would `PUT` the previous analyzer and silently rename it.

**The dangerous half is fixed, and it is fixed the right way round.** Two paths were driven:

- **Close and reopen.** Fill step 1, run through Verify and Connect, close the panel with **X**,
  click **Add Analyzer** → clean step 1: analyzer type empty, name empty, lab units empty, steps 2
  and 3 greyed. Correct.
- **Panel already open** (the original repro). Opened `?setup=instrument&analyzerId=4` on
  *QuantStudio 7* and clicked **Add Analyzer** twice. The URL **keeps** `analyzerId=4`, and the
  fields keep *QuantStudio 7*'s name and type. Nothing resets — **and nothing pretends to.**

That second reading is the important one. The panel no longer sheds `analyzerId` while holding the
previous analyzer's data, so it no longer *looks* like a new analyzer while *being* the old one.
Continue from that state issues `PUT …/4`, which is now the correct thing to do, because the URL
and the fields both say you are editing analyzer 4. **The silent-rename risk is gone.**

**What is left is a smaller UX defect:** with a setup panel open, **Add Analyzer does nothing at
all** — no reset, no new panel, no message, no visual change. A user who wants to add a second
instrument right after inspecting the first will click it, see nothing happen, and have no
indication that they must close the panel first. Severity **minor / UX**, no data risk. Worth a
fix in the same pass, since the button either belongs disabled with a tooltip or should reset the
panel outright.

### Δ-K — no data-flow control **— FIXED, retested 2026-08-27**
Reported as: the connection block declares `transport`, `connectionRole`, `host` and `port` — who
opens the socket and over what — but no field for FR-F's *Results only (one-way)* versus *Two-way
(send orders/queries)*, so AC-10 could not be satisfied as written.
**Now fixed, and both halves of AC-10 are evidenced.** Step 3 *Connect* renders a **Data flow**
control (`analyzer-connection-dataFlow`), and it follows what the profile declares rather than
offering a free choice:

- **Bruker FluoroCycler XT (FILE).** `RESULTS_ONLY` alone — correct, a drop-folder instrument
  cannot receive orders.
- **Cepheid GeneXpert (ASTM, `communicationMode: BOTH`).** `RESULTS_ONLY` **and** `TWO_WAY`
  (rendered *"Results only"* / *"Two-way"*) — which is FR-F2's choice, present at last.

The two-way half was recorded as untested after the manual pass and was picked up by the automated
run, which drives the first analyzer in the list. Closed.

Also improved in the same area: **Test connection now returns evidence rather than a bare failure.**
A bad directory yields *"Connection failed"* with *"Directory: The configured directory was not
found."*

### Δ-Y — "my instrument isn't listed" reaches Create Profile, which is a dead end

The escape hatch exists (round 1's Δ-D is fixed) but cannot be completed. **Create Profile collects
only a name**, then reports *"Profile draft created — the draft is saved in Analyzer Bridge. It must
be completed and validated before it can be published for analyzer setup."* There is no editor, no
Publish action, and the draft never appears in the Analyzer Types list. Re-opening
`?action=create&draft={uuid}` shows the same terminal message.

**Updated 2026-08-27.** The message above is new and is a real improvement — the earlier build
failed silently. The behaviour behind it is unchanged. The draft exists server-side, is fetchable at
`/analyzer-types/drafts/{id}`, is absent from the catalog, and the server names exactly what a
publishable profile needs:

```
POST /rest/analyzer-types/drafts/{id}/publish → 400
  "Profile draft cannot be published: $.profileMeta: required property 'confidence' not found;
   $.profileMeta: required property 'version' not found; $: required property 'capabilities'
   not found; $: required property 'category' not found; $: required property 'configDefaults'
   not found; $: required property 'connectionFields' not found; $: required property
   'controlResultRecognition' not found; $: required property 'protocol' not found"
```

So FR-B3's protocol and connection type do **not** appear downstream — they are required by the
Bridge contract and nothing in OpenELIS collects them. The backend is well specified and validates
properly; **this is a UI gap.** A deployment can currently only fork an existing type, never author
a new one — and per Δ-AA, the fork does not carry the work either.

### Δ-AA — Duplicate Profile forks the shipped profile, not the site binding, so the fork loses every mapping decision and every site-learned value **(new, 2026-08-27)**

This supersedes the *"Duplicate Profile works, and it is the FR-H fork"* section in the 2026-08-25
draft. The mechanics do work — the modal is honest about semantics, `POST …/duplicate` → **201**
opens a real draft editor, `POST …/drafts/{id}/publish` → **201** publishes, and the result lands in
the list as *Site-created · Derived from genexpert-astm revision 4*. **What does not survive is the
work.**

Duplicated *Cepheid GeneXpert (ASTM Mode) revision 4* through the UI and compared source to copy
seconds later:

| | Source `genexpert-astm` rev 4 | The copy, on publish |
|---|---|---|
| Tests | 4, all `BOUND` (testIds 395, 396, 313, 300) | 4, all `UNRESOLVED`, `testId: null` |
| Result values | 17 — 10 `BOUND`, 6 `EXCLUDED`, 1 `UNRESOLVED` | 16 — every one `UNRESOLVED` |
| Summary state | `COMPLETE` | `NOT_STARTED` / `NEEDS_LOCAL_MAPPING` |

**One mechanism explains both columns: Duplicate forks the *shipped profile*, not the *site
binding*.**

That was not obvious at first. The initial reading was "the copy loses the bindings, and separately
drops the `UNRESOLVED` value" — two problems. A later fork settled it. By then `REVIEW REQUIRED` on
MTB-RIF had been mapped and confirmed, so it was **`BOUND`** in the source, not unresolved — and a
fresh fork **still omitted it**:

```
missing in copy: MTB-RIF / "REVIEW REQUIRED (BOUND, observed)"
```

So the rule has nothing to do with `mappingState`. `REVIEW REQUIRED` is a value the instance
*learned from traffic* (`observed: true`); the shipped profile does not declare it. Everything the
site added or bound lives on the site binding, and the fork does not read the site binding at all.
Hence:

**1. Every mapping decision is discarded**, because the decisions are site-binding state. The modal
promises *"New profile with preserved lineage. The new profile starts from Cepheid GeneXpert (ASTM
Mode) revision 4."* `parentProfileId` and `parentRevision` are preserved; the 20 test and result
decisions are not. FR-H exists so a lab can fork a working type to give one analyzer different
behaviour — forking currently means redoing all 20 bindings by hand.

**2. Site-learned values disappear**, because they too are site-binding state. `REVIEW REQUIRED` is
the value that held `DEV01261000000000003`; 17 values become 16. A lab that forks a profile to deal
with a problem value gets a profile that cannot express that value at all. Reproduced on the three
site-created duplicates already in the seed and on two forks made during this run.

If forking the shipped profile is deliberate, the modal copy is actively misleading and the FRS
should say which of the two artefacts FR-H means. If it is not deliberate, the fix is to fork the
site binding.

**FR-H is therefore only partly satisfied:** the fork mechanism ships and publishes cleanly, but it
does not carry the state that makes forking worth doing.

Minor, carried forward from the 2026-08-25 observation: each profile action fires its POST **twice**
on a single click (duplicate 2×, publish 2×). The same `draftId` comes back both times, so it
appears idempotent, but the double submit is worth a look.

### Δ-AB — the Analyzer Types list's mapping counts are stale, and call a profile `COMPLETE` while it is holding patient results **(new, 2026-08-27)**

*Cepheid GeneXpert (ASTM Mode)* had two held results at the time of the reading. The list row said:

> **Results mapped** 10 / 16 · 63% · 6 marked Do not receive — **Status** Active, no attention flag

The mapping detail page for the same profile said **10 / 17**. The discrepancy is not a rounding
artefact; the two surfaces count different things:

```
GET /analyzer-types                → resultMappings { mapped 10, excluded 6, total 16, state COMPLETE }
GET /analyzer-types/genexpert-astm/mapping?revision=4
                                   → 17 values: 10 BOUND, 6 EXCLUDED, 1 UNRESOLVED
```

At that moment the reading looked like a denominator rule: **`UNRESOLVED` values excluded from the
numerator, the denominator and the state**, so the one row that needs attention is the one that does
not count.

**The real defect is worse than that: the catalog is stale.** After binding `REVIEW REQUIRED` and
confirming the mapping — `PUT …/mapping?revision=4` **200**, `siteBindingRevision` 2 → 3,
`POST …/mapping/confirm` **200**, confirmation `CURRENT`, mapping now **11 `BOUND` + 6 `EXCLUDED` =
17 with zero unresolved** — a **cache-busted** `GET /analyzer-types` still returned
`{ mapped 10, excluded 6, total 16, COMPLETE }`. The automated suite re-read it again some hours
later and got the identical pre-change numbers:

```
[Δ-AB] mapping {"BOUND":11,"EXCLUDED":6} total=17
     · catalog {"mapped":10,"excluded":6,"total":16,"state":"COMPLETE"}
```

So the denominator quirk was only the shape the disagreement happened to have while a value was
unresolved. **The catalog counts do not track the site binding at all** — they still describe the
profile as it was before the lab touched it, indefinitely. A profile whose every remaining value is
unresolved would still read `N / N · 100% · COMPLETE`, and mapping work never shows up here.

Related, same root: the **Needs Attention** KPI on Analyzer Types counts only `NOT_STARTED`
profiles. `genexpert-astm` — the only profile actually blocking clinical results — is not among
them, while three unused site-created duplicates are.

**Consequence.** A supervisor scanning Analyzer Types to answer *"is our mapping healthy?"* gets a
confidently wrong answer, and gets no feedback that the mapping work they just did landed. This is
worse than an incomplete view, because it reads as reassurance.

Severity: **Medium-High.**

### Δ-AC — an analyzer code the profile does not declare has no resolution path **(new, 2026-08-27)**

Two held results sit on the GeneXpert page and look identical to a user — both **Held**, both
**REVIEW REQUIRED**, both showing an *Analyzer code* line. The payload distinguishes them, and only
one of the two gets a route out:

| Accession | `importIssueReason` | Analyzer code | Resolution offered |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEV01261000000000003` | `unknown_analyzer_result_value` | `MTB-RIF` (declared, value unknown) | **Review Analyzer Type mapping** link, working deep link |
| `DEV01261000000000002` | `unknown_analyzer_test` | `UNMAPPED-MTB` (not declared at all) | **nothing** — no link, no `testId`, no route |

The mapping page for `genexpert-astm` lists only the four declared codes (MTB-RIF, RIF, HIV-VL,
COVID19) and offers **no add-code control**; `UNMAPPED-MTB` is absent from the mapping payload
entirely. So the server knows precisely which of the two failure modes it is looking at, and the UI
branches for only one of them.

The banner copy — *"Held results cannot be accepted. Resolve the Analyzer Type mapping so the next
matching result can enter the normal review workflow"* — is accurate and much better than the
previous build's, but it does not apply to this row: there is no mapping to resolve. The lab's only
options are to ignore the result or ask the vendor to change the shipped profile.

This is a **missing UI branch, not missing data** — which is what makes it cheap to fix.

### Δ-AD — a confirmed mapping change is not audited **(new, 2026-08-27)**

Made a real change and confirmed it: `REVIEW REQUIRED` → `INDETERMINATE`, `PUT
/analyzer-types/genexpert-astm/mapping?revision=4` **200**, banner flipped to *"Confirmation is
stale"*, `POST …/mapping/confirm?revision=4` **200**, banner then read *"Confirmed by Open ELIS on
Aug 27, 2026, 1:23 PM"*. `siteBindingRevision` advanced **2 → 3**.

Row menu → **View history** still shows only:

```
Revision 1 · Active · Shipped · distribution · Aug 18, 2026, 5:00 PM
Revision 2 · Active · Shipped · distribution · Aug 25, 2026, 5:00 PM
Revision 3 · Active · Shipped · distribution · Aug 25, 2026, 6:00 PM
Revision 4 · Active · Shipped · distribution · Aug 25, 2026, 7:00 PM
```

The change made minutes earlier does not appear. The site binding **is** versioned server-side —
`siteBindingRevision` proves it — but the dialog lists *shipped-profile* revisions instead of
*site-binding* revisions. **Nothing in the UI records who changed a mapping, or when.**

For a clinical LIMS that is the wrong default: a mapping change silently alters how every future
result from that instrument is interpreted, and it is exactly the thing an inspector asks to see a
trail for. The data is already there; this is a dialog reading the wrong series.

Severity: **Medium** for the MVP, **High** for any production deployment.

### Δ-Z — results carry provenance in the payload but the UI shows it only on held rows **(revised 2026-08-27)**

As first reported, a result arriving from an analyzer reached normal review carrying only the token
`AUTO` in a column titled *Analyzer Result*, with the analyzer never named — confirmed on two
analyzers and two protocols.

**The data half is fixed.** Every result row now carries real provenance:

```
sourceProfileId: "genexpert-astm"   sourceProfileRevision: 4
sourceProtocol:  "ASTM"             sourceTransport: "TCP"
rawTestCode:     "MTB-RIF"          importIssueReason: "unknown_analyzer_result_value"
```

**The rendering half is not.** The UI prints an *Analyzer code: …* line only on **Held** rows. The
accepted `MTB-RIF / NOT DETECTED` row shows Sample Info, Test Name, Result, Test Date and nothing
else — no analyzer, no protocol, no raw code. The live-traffic story's step 1 expects *"the NOT
DETECTED patient result appears in normal review with analyzer and source context"*, and fails on
exactly that clause.

Downstream clinical screens were not re-tested this round; the finding as stated is scoped to the
analyzer results view. Since the payload already carries everything needed, this is a small render
change rather than a data change.

### Δ-W — the pickers jump to a match but never narrow the list **— FIXED, both controls, retested 2026-08-27**
Reported as: both Carbon ComboBoxes accepted text and neither filtered — the analyzer-type picker
held its option count for any query, the per-row test picker at 183 before and 183 after. What they
did instead was jump to the match and highlight it.

**Both now filter.**
- **Analyzer-type picker.** Typing `Fluo` narrows 7 options to 1, *Bruker FluoroCycler XT*.
- **Mapping-page test picker.** Typing `Hemato` narrows **183 to 1**. LOINC search still works.

A note on how the second reading was obtained, because it changes the confidence: the manual retest
could not drive focus into the mapping picker (see the banner note under Minor), so it was recorded
as **not re-tested** rather than guessed at, and the QA suite's old jump-don't-filter assertion was
left in place and flagged. The automated run then failed that assertion — *"Expected: 183,
Received: 1"* — which is the flip-when-fixed mechanism doing exactly its job. The assertion has been
flipped to a guard. Closed.

### Minor
- The Port field shows "This field is required" while holding a value, until blurred.
- **New.** The held-results banner on the Analyzers list is a Carbon `ActionableNotification`
  rendered with `hideCloseButton`, and it takes focus when it mounts. For a short window after it
  renders, clicks and `focus()` calls on other controls get pulled back to its action button —
  enough to swallow a first attempt at typing into the analyzer name field. It settles, and
  **Escape** dismisses the banner entirely, so it is not a hard block; but there is no visible way
  to dismiss it and it competes for focus on the page where the setup wizard lives.
- **New.** The QC Dashboard's *Type* column prints the raw profile slug (`genexpert-astm`) rather
  than a display name.
- **New.** FluoroCycler results render with no units on a quantitative viral-load value.
- **New, housekeeping.** The in-app review widget lists this run's story source as **OGC-1054**
  rather than OGC-1057, and gives no confirmation after **Submit review** — the button stays
  enabled and the counter unchanged, so a submitter cannot tell whether the POST landed.

**Withdrawn from this section:** *"the analyzer-scoped QC page displayed In Control for an analyzer
with no control lot"* and *"the QC Dashboard reports No instruments found"*. Both were empty-state
readings taken before any QC data existed, not defects. With a control result present the QC
Dashboard populates correctly — Cepheid GeneXpert (ASTM Mode), Biochemistry, **In Control**, analyte
HIV Viral Load(Serum), **0.0σ**, no violations, Instruments In Control 1, Overall QC Pass Rate 100%
— and the analyzer-scoped page shows the same reading with a control chart. Retested 2026-08-26 and
again 2026-08-27.

  list, Add creates a new analyzer correctly. The real, narrower finding was Δ-S, now fixed.

  correctly, and the panel raises *"Select at least one lab unit"*. The first look missed the notice.
- **"The held-results banner traps keyboard focus."** Raised and withdrawn within the 2026-08-27
  run. On a freshly loaded page with the banner present, `focus()` succeeds on every setup field.
  The real, narrower behaviour is the transient focus-steal recorded under Minor.

## What works and should not be allowed to regress

The re-baselined suite guards these explicitly, with assertions that are *not* flip-when-fixed:

- Bound mapping rows resolve to a catalog test object, not a name hint; every code carries a
  `mappingState`; `controlRecognition` is present.
- The mapping is a versioned, fingerprinted **site binding**, so a lab's change never edits the
  shipped profile.
- The confirmation is pinned to both the binding and the recognition fingerprint — the mechanism
  that makes staling work at all.
- No QC blocker appears in `activation-readiness`.
- The connection schema drives field visibility from the server (`host` appears only when the role
  is `CLIENT`; `connectionRole` only when transport is not RS-232).
- The probe is real and its outcome is persisted against a `configRevision`.
- The row menu offers Deactivate/Reactivate and **no Delete**.
- Held results are kept out of clinical review and retained on the analyzer page; a recognized
  control is routed to operational QC with a z-score and creates no patient accession; FILE results
  post with the right values and no import plumbing exposed.
- The deep link from a held row to the mapping page carries `revision`, `returnTo`, `focusTest` and
  `focusValue`, opens the right accordion row and tags the value *Observed in held results*.

---

## Design questions for the PO (not defects)

- **Create Profile collects only a name.** FR-B3 specifies protocol and connection type at this
  point; on 3.2.2.0 they are defined outside OpenELIS. The path is reachable, but a lab admin
  cannot finish the job in this UI. Confirm the split is intended, and amend FR-B3 if so.
- **Is Duplicate Profile meant to start empty?** See Δ-AA. Either the copy should carry the source's
  bindings, or the modal should stop saying the new profile "starts from" the source.
- **A held result is never released by fixing the mapping.** After binding and confirming
  `REVIEW REQUIRED`, `DEV01261000000000003` stayed held. That matches the banner's *"so the next
  matching result can enter the normal review workflow"*, so it reads as intended — but it means the
  held result that motivated the fix can only be cleared by re-running the specimen. For a patient
  sample that is a real cost. Confirm this is the intent, and if so say it in the UI.
- **The analyzer-scoped QC link opens a monitoring view** (Activity Timeline / Control Chart).
  Control-lot and Westgard configuration live in the sidebar, so the QC step of setup cannot be
  completed from the analyzer link itself.

---

## Not tested

- **Operational QC end to end**, because Δ-R makes it unreachable — with no control lot and no
  Westgard rule, "changing QC does not stale the mapping confirmation or add activation blockers"
  could not be verified in either direction.
- **Downstream clinical screens for analyzer provenance** — see Δ-Z. The payload carries everything
  needed; only the analyzer results view was re-checked.
- **The re-send half of the live-traffic story.** Closing it needs the demo operator to send
  `GeneXpert / MTB-RIF / REVIEW REQUIRED` again; there is no analyzer-mock control inside OpenELIS
  and `35.85.196.163:9600` refuses external connections.
- **Learn-from-traffic** (FR-B7/B8, FR-G) and everything downstream of an ACTIVE analyzer:
  reconciliation against the mappings, pending codes, pending result values. **This is the gap
  between M3 and a reportable module.**
- Mobile / responsive.
